Cc: Raj Patel <raj@nimbushealth.com>, procurement@nimbushealth.com

Subject: Post-call: SLO/throughput handoff & reproducibility checklist

Hi Samira — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope the qualification run: 

Recap
- Primary use case: realtime triage suggestions in clinician UI (short sequences, streaming session support)
- Expected peak concurrent users: ~350 active sessions, avg session length ~18s of generation
- Latency targets requested on call: p50 ~50-70ms, p95 <300ms for online inference

What we need from your side to make the benchmark reproducible
1) Confirm target SLOs you want validated (p50/p95/p99 where relevant)
2) Provide a traffic sample (jsonl) that matches production sampling (we attached a template and an example harness config)
3) Any streaming/session semantics to reproduce (e.g., partial-token flush, gap between user utterances, user-id affinity)
4) Network topology constraints (will requests originate from Nimbus VPC in us-west-2?)

We attached: Redwood_Benchmark_Template.xlsx (measurement columns we’ll publish) and initial-harness-config.yml (runtime flags we’ll use).

Proposed schedule
- Share traffic sample + signed NDA (if needed): by EOD 3/12
- Redwood to run smoke tests and share methodology: 3/13
- Full qualification run (sustained concurrency + streaming sessions): target 3/15-3/16

Can you confirm the p95 target you want us to validate and whether the traffic sample we need can be provided as jsonl? If procurement needs a statement of work or SC access, loop them in and we’ll provide.

Thanks — I’ll also loop in our benchmarking lead (Ben) and product CS (Monica) for the measurement defs.

Best,
Michael Grant
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwoodinference.com

Thanks Michael — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications and an initial traffic sample attached.

Preliminary SLOs (internal expectations):
- p50 target: 60ms (we can accept 50-70ms range)
- p95 target: 280ms
- p99: soft target: 500ms (not required for go/no-go but helpful to surface)

Streaming semantics
- Client sends partial tokens every 100-150ms; server should support chunked streaming with per-session ordering guarantees
- Sessions are sticky to a user-id for the duration of a clinical encounter (persisted KV cache between messages)

Traffic sample: attached nimbus_traffic_sample.jsonl (2000 lines, mixed short and medium prompts). The sample is sanitized.

We are in us-west-2 for inference egress; we can provide a private test subnet if needed. Procurement is copied for SOW/NDAs.

Next steps: we can share an S3 location for larger samples if you need more than the attached file — let us know by EOD tomorrow. Also available for a short follow-up to align streaming flush behavior.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2027-03-12T09:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: SLO/throughput handoff & reproducibility checklist

Internal: proposed measurement/benchmark plan to share with Nimbus once they confirm samples/NDA.

High-level benchmark phases (suggested)
1) Smoke + validation (1 hour)
   - Verify harness can replay sample, validate tokenization parity, KV caching behavior
   - Baseline p50/p95 with single-node config and debug traces
2) Sustained concurrency (3-4 hours)
   - Ramp to 350 concurrent sessions; measure distribution across p50/p95/p99 and error rates
   - Collect token-level traces for long-tail analysis
3) Streaming session test (2 hours)
   - Simulate partial-token flush every 120ms and mid-session context growth to ~1k tokens
   - Verify per-session ordering and KV cache reuse across messages

Measurement definitions (to pin)
- p50/p95/p99 as observed at the Redwood API edge (time from request arrival to first-byte of model output)
- Throughput measured in queries-per-second (qps) and active sessions per second
- Error taxonomy: timeouts, server-err (5xx), user-abort (client disconnect)

Repro checklist to ask Nimbus for
- sanitized traffic sample (jsonl) + mapping to real traffic mix
- environment: VPC region, expected network egress path, any ingress routing that could add latency
- expected concurrency distribution map (counts by minute/hour)

If that looks good I’ll draft a short runbook (public-facing) that we can send to Samira with the measurement defs and the exact harness commands. Also recommend we run the smoke and streaming tests during off-peak to avoid production interference.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Benchmarking Lead, Redwood Inference
